items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was having all these problems with Joe on the road... I could see flaws in him that I couldn't see before. He was so magnificent as a musician, a drummer.

ctx.x: Let’s go back to the Jazz Workshop. You mentioned how important it was to you. Was this indicative of Jack McDuff? Was he touring a lot?

Jack worked constantly, and he set the tone for me. I used to work somewhere between 45 and 48 weeks a year. Jack worked about the same, constantly. We didn’t make any money, but we worked all the time. I was the only one that had money in my pocket, because I had no vices. Those cats used to borrow money from me, which I charged them 6% interest. They hated me on payday. I said, “Man, where’s my $30, Joe?” Joe would whisper under his breath, “You jive – here’s your money.” “Listen, man, don’t play with my money.…

And every time he got in trouble, you know I had to respond. The man saved me from going to the penitentiary. So somebody told me, “Hey, George, they arrested Jack on the turnpike. They got him down there.” I said, “Where is he at?” I jumped in my big 600 limousine. Went down there. Had to fight with the police – not literally anymore. I don’t do that no more. I got great lawyers. They said, “Just sit down in that corner right there.” I said, “I’ve been sitting here 45 minutes, and you told me he’d be down in 15…
